title: Google Releases Angular v22 with Stable Signal Forms, OnPush by Default and Experimental WebMCP
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/angular-v22-released/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1786119245139.jpg"/><p>Angular v22, Google's TypeScript-first framework, has introduced API stabilizations, ergonomic templates, and tooling enhancements for AI integration. Key developments include the stabilization of Signal Forms, improved change detection strategies, and a new @Service() decorator for dependency injection. The release supports TypeScript 6 and removes deprecated features.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: eslint-rspack-plugin 5.0.0 Ships as a Pure ESM Package, Aligning with the Rstack Ecosystem
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/eslint-rspack-plugin-5/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1785692458963.jpg"/><p>Version 5.0.0 of eslint-rspack-plugin has been released as a pure ESM package, aligning with the Rspack ecosystem and removing its CommonJS build. The plugin continues to integrate ESLint in the build process but may affect build times. Users are advised to consider separate linting commands for efficiency. The project is open source and available via npm.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Microsoft Releases TypeScript 7.0 with a Native Go Compiler, Delivering 10x Faster Builds
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/typescript-7-released/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1785691904681.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released TypeScript 7.0, featuring a native compiler that improves build speeds by 8x to 12x. Notable performance enhancements were evidenced in real codebases. The version lacks a stable programmatic API, anticipated in 7.1. Transitioning includes a compatibility package for existing tooling, and TypeScript remains an open-source project.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
